negative_findings.description: No formal, incorporated fintech association with a public member directory was found for North Macedonia. Searches in mk and en returned only informal community pages (Fintech MK on Medium/Facebook), the regional Balkan Fintech Association, and the alternative-lenders body AFD.
negative_findings.result_summary: Fintech representation in MK appears to sit inside MASIT, the Economic Chamber's non-bank financial group, and the e-commerce association rather than in a standalone fintech chamber.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any expectation of a single fintech member census for MK is unfounded; the fintech actor map must be assembled from MASIT + mchamber groups + ecommerce.mk.

negative_findings.description: MBA's website confirms the membership composition (all banks and savings houses, plus KIBS clearing house and the Macedonian Credit Bureau) but a clean per-institution member page was not located in this run; the count cited (14 banks, 2 savings houses) derives from a 2020-dated statement.
negative_findings.result_summary: Membership is stated narratively rather than as a maintained structured directory.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The bank census should be reconciled against the National Bank's licensed-institutions register rather than taken from MBA text alone; MBA figures may be stale.

negative_findings.description: Searched in mk and en for MASIT position papers on banking/digital transformation; only news-format advocacy items (e.g. on formalising the economy through digital solutions) were found, not a documents/publications library.
negative_findings.result_summary: Advocacy output appears distributed through the news feed rather than a dedicated policy-paper section.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection must monitor the news feeds continuously; a one-off scrape of a 'publications' page will find nothing.

negative_findings.description: Albanian-language association and chamber sources (notably the Chamber of Commerce of NW Macedonia / Oda Ekonomike e Maqedonisë Veriperëndimore) were not searched, because Albanian is outside the run's declared languages (mk, en).
negative_findings.result_summary: A material part of the MK business-association ecosystem publishes primarily in Albanian and was left uncovered.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Vendor and member lists for the Albanian-language business community are likely under-represented in this slice.

negative_findings.description: Domains for the NW Macedonia chamber (oemvp.org) and the Union of Chambers (chamber.mk) were inferred from organisational identity and social-media handles rather than confirmed by a successful fetch in this run.
negative_findings.result_summary: Recorded with low confidence and flagged as unverified rather than omitted or asserted as live.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Downstream liveness verification must resolve these before they enter the tracked-source register.

brief: North Macedonia's association layer is small, concentrated and unusually collectable: MASIT (masit.org.mk) offers a paginated ICT member directory of ~80+ vendors with per-company profile pages, and the Macedonian Banking Association (mba.mk) covers the entire licensed banking demand side plus KIBS and the Credit Bureau, publishing committee rosters, quarterly e-bulletins and the SKIBOR reference-bank panel. The Economic Chamber of North Macedonia (mchamber.mk) adds cross-sector groupings — financial organisations, non-bank financial companies, insurance brokers — that widen the buyer map beyond banks, while ecommerce.mk supplies a payments-side merchant register and steady coverage of instant payments and SEPA accession. There is no standalone incorporated fintech association with a public member list; fintech representation is dispersed across MASIT, the chamber's non-bank group, the alternative-lenders body AFD, and the regional Balkan Fintech Association. Highest-yield future collection is event-driven — association forums, MoUs (e.g. MASIT–SETPE Digital Bridge 2026) and sponsor lists surface partnerships well before contracts appear; the main blind spots are Albanian-language chamber sources and historical roster depth.
